title: 실제 시연 관찰 안내 — 기존108문단 보존

scenes.title: 02-p1 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Let us inspect that first stage in a Robo Recall diagnostic view. Diagnostic colors replace the usual material appearance to reveal overlapping drawing. As the camera moves, the visible overlap of walls and railings changes. These colors do not represent light intensity. We are separating visibility from lighting the visible surface.

scenes.title: 02-p2 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Now inspect an isolated wall. A broad face in the front view becomes a thin edge from the side because the relation between camera and object has changed. Projecting triangles requires those positions and depths. Whether the wall is metallic and which light reaches it are separate questions. This diagnostic view does not by itself reveal the GPU’s complete execution order.

scenes.title: 04-p1 · steam-quake-enhanced-2021
lines: As the viewpoint moves, the pattern stays attached to the surface. Keep its texture coordinates distinct from the coordinates used to store lighting.

scenes.title: 04-p5 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: The numbers in each room identify the displayed comparison conditions. First inspect the wall pattern, then the boundary where a shadow crosses it. The two kinds of detail need not be stored at the same density.

scenes.title: 04-p6 · bethesda-quake2-enhanced-2023
lines: Inspect texture sharpness separately from lighting-edge sharpness.

scenes.title: 04-p7 · bethesda-quake2-enhanced-2023
lines: Even a dark passage need not have a uniform color. Its appearance alone does not identify the algorithm used to compute indirect lighting.

scenes.title: 04-p8 · bethesda-quake2-enhanced-2023
lines: A similar visual impression and an identical calculation method are different claims.

scenes.title: 04-p9 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: Here the viewpoint travels along wall junctions. Compare the broad surface with the seam. A visible boundary can have several causes, including sample density and surface partitioning. Identifying the cause requires the stored data and production settings as well. Camera movement itself is not evidence of a new bake.

scenes.title: 04-p10 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: This is object manipulation in the editor, not a completed light-off and rebake comparison.

scenes.title: 04-p3 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: Carry the same question between rooms: which detail is the wall pattern, and which is a broad lighting variation? If lighting was computed before play, the runtime needs an address for finding the stored result. That is the role of the separate lightmap in our diagram.

scenes.title: 04-p11 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: Moving the camera does not make stored lighting samples follow it. A moving object must retrieve values appropriate to its own location. Shortly we will compare samples on a wall with samples distributed through space.

scenes.title: 04f-p1 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Viewed obliquely, distant road details crowd into a narrow part of the image. Selecting one texel as if it were a nearby surface cannot adequately represent that larger region.

scenes.title: 04f-p2 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Smaller mip levels combine fine details. The purpose is to choose values representing the sampled region, not to select a blurry image arbitrarily.

scenes.title: 04f-p4 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: A texture can hold data other than photographic color. This view separates masks packed into different channels. Red, green and blue do not automatically identify a normal map. Before interpreting filtering, identify what the blended values actually mean.

scenes.title: 04f-p6 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Follow the thin fire-escape edges. Their width in the image changes with the viewpoint. Stabilizing a distant thin structure resembles texture sampling, but the problems are not identical. Texture filters handle the region read from stored detail. How much of a pixel an actual triangle edge covers is a question about image samples. The later Forward example connects this to testing edges with multiple samples.

scenes.title: 04t-p1 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Tilting the camera toward the building changes the geometry covering the image. Classifying those triangles by the image region they affect is the starting point for our tile explanation. This engine view is not an execution trace of historical PowerVR hardware.

scenes.title: 07-p1 · steam-doom3-original
lines: Inspect the lit surfaces from the moving viewpoint.

scenes.title: 07-p4 · steam-doom3-original
lines: While moving, distinguish surface brightness from the object’s silhouette. The next diagram constructs the space behind that boundary.

scenes.title: 07-p8 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Now inspect a robot surface in a more recent engine. Separate the outer silhouette from small variations inside it. Painted color, material reflection and surface orientation can all affect the image. A bumpy appearance does not prove that the vertices have moved into the same shape. This distinction leads into normals and stored lighting.

scenes.title: 08-p1 · steam-hl2-legacy-trailer
lines: Notice the impression that the character and background occupy one space. That does not mean static walls and moving characters must retrieve lighting from the same storage. We will separate directional components from spatial samples.

scenes.title: 08-p5 · steam-hl2-current-trailer
lines: In a game, camera and object motion can combine several changes. Isolating the effect of normals therefore requires a controlled diagram. Compare the bright and dark detail within materials with their outer silhouette. A richer way to read stored illumination does not automatically create every moving object’s occlusion. Connect the finished scene to the calculation without guessing invisible implementation details.

scenes.title: 08-p6 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Here we inspect the robot’s arm and torso from different directions. The outline gives clues about geometry, while small variations inside a face give clues about material and orientation. Treating them as the same thing overstates what normal maps can do. Our earlier diagram changed directions without moving the plane’s vertices. Apply the same habit of separating outline from interior detail here.

scenes.title: 08-p7 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: Look at the positions of the displayed points. They occupy the room rather than forming a wall-texture grid. Selecting the character lets us inspect the spatial relation between it and the samples. A moving object needs lighting information for its new location. This follows our Half-Life2 discussion, but the Unreal demonstration is a separate engine example, not the same storage format.

scenes.title: 08-p8 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: First inspect the character together with the surrounding sample visualization. Locate the prepared values, then follow the character as it changes position. It cannot carry a single wall texel around the room; it needs lighting information appropriate to its location.

The room interior and the floor outside have different surroundings and incoming illumination. As the character moves between them, inspect its body brightness together with its position. The displayed samples are spatial clues for this lookup, not necessarily actual light sources.

Later, a changed viewpoint reveals the samples and object from another direction. Two points close in the image may be separated in depth. Unlike a surface lightmap, this distribution must be read in height as well. These operations do not measure exact interpolation weights or per-frame cost. Internal values require separate engine evidence.

scenes.title: 08-p9 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: For an editor, the question is not merely whether the image is bright or dark, but what must be recomputed after a change. This room and wall inspection is part of scene authoring. It is not a baking benchmark, and its playback duration is not a computation-time measurement.

scenes.title: 08-p4 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Inspect the changes in object position and orientation a little longer. First identify the face presented to the camera, then follow its pattern and shading. Also distinguish object motion from camera motion.

Our diagram changed only a normal direction to isolate one input. Several conditions may change together in a real editor. A brighter patch therefore does not reveal a numerical increase in a particular lightmap component. Keep the three stages connected: surface orientation, stored data and the retrieved result.

scenes.title: 08-p3 · steam-hl2-legacy-trailer
lines: The final image does not display directional lighting components separately. The game shows the result; the diagram separates the intermediate values producing it. Reading them together makes the storage scheme meaningful.

scenes.title: 08-p8 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: Finally inspect the room from another viewpoint. Consider sample placement together with the places a character can occupy. The existence of samples does not make lighting exact everywhere. Their density, placement and interpolation are further design choices. The key here is that storage is in space rather than on the wall.

scenes.title: 09a-p8 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: The colored boundaries visualize shadow-recording regions, not additional lights.

scenes.title: 09a-p9 · epic-lighting-techniques-2017
lines: Inspect near and far regions together. The total distance and distribution change as well as the number of splits. Connect each visible setting change with the affected region instead of drawing a conclusion from one still image.

scenes.title: 09b-p3 · epic-material-baking-2017
lines: Unwrapping the book places information from different faces onto one plane, relating the original three-dimensional surfaces to texture addresses. This does not mean storing only final lighting brightness. Separate data such as base color and roughness by their meaning. The export process then demonstrates handling those surface data independently.

scenes.title: 09b-p2 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Here we inspect Robo Recall material data. Channel masks distinguish surface properties. Their colors do not automatically represent final display color or normals. In Deferred shading, the important question is not just the number of buffers, but what each value represents and what the next stage reads.

scenes.title: 09b-p10 · epic-robo-recall-announce-2016
lines: This is actual VR interaction with objects. Inspect both the response and the image edges.

scenes.title: 09b-p10 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: In the game running from the editor, hands, robots and fragments move together. A clear image requires more than material brightness: thin structures and moving outlines must also be sampled. This is an example of real renderer inputs, not evidence of a particular frame rate.

scenes.title: 09b-p10 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: The comparison magnifies edges while handling multisample settings. First locate the enlarged line in the original image. A single image sample may not adequately distinguish the area covered by a thin triangle. Testing coverage at multiple positions can represent the boundary differently.

The magnified change alone does not establish a speedup. Sample count, resolution, materials and scene conditions all matter. Observe the console operations and edge changes without inferring unreadable settings. This is a case of choosing a Forward path by considering quality, required features and cost together.

scenes.title: 09b-p11 · epic-robo-performance-2017
lines: Changing diagnostic modes reveals information otherwise combined in the final image. This reflection view is not automatically screen-space reflection. Even when effect names resemble one another, their inputs and implementation must be identified.
